title: A New Snake Just Got Named After a Rock Star
summary:
Imagine you're a scientist, and you find a snake nobody has ever seen before. What would you name it? One team named theirs after a rock star.

The snake is a reddish-brown groundsnake about 28 inches long — roughly as long as a baseball bat. It was found in the forests of New Guinea, a huge tropical island just north of Australia. Its new name is Lielaphis slashi, which means "Slash's groundsnake."

Who's Slash? He's the famous guitarist for the band Guns N' Roses. But here's the surprise: he's also been crazy about reptiles his whole life. He has supported zoos and museums for years. When he heard the news, he said he was "extremely honored and humbled."

The scientist who named the snake is Sara Ruane from the Field Museum. She loved Guns N' Roses since first grade. When she was twelve, she saw Slash on a magazine cover holding his pet python. She thought, "This guy is so cool." He talked about hunting for snakes as a kid — just like she did.

How do scientists know it's a new species? They studied its DNA (the instructions inside living things) and counted its scales. Both were different from similar snakes. The snake hunts at night, near big trees, looking for lizards and reptile eggs to eat.

So a guitar hero now has a snake named after him. Not bad!
why_it_matters: Carefully studying even a small animal like a snake can reveal a brand-new species — and the curiosity you use to look closely at nature now is the same curiosity that can become a job you love later.

background_read: New Guinea (a big tropical island just north of Australia) is one of the wildest places on Earth — it has tree kangaroos, birds of paradise and dozens of kinds of snakes.
Slash (the lead guitarist of the rock band Guns N' Roses, which became famous in the 1980s) has loved snakes since he was a boy and has helped zoos and museums that take care of reptiles.
Scientists often name new species after famous people, and it can help more people notice animals that need protecting.
Article_Structure: WHO: A team of scientists led by Sara Ruane at the Field Museum, plus the rock star Slash, who the snake is named after.
WHAT: They discovered a brand-new snake species and named it Lielaphis slashi — 'Slash's groundsnake.'
WHERE: In the forests of New Guinea, a huge tropical island just north of Australia.
WHY: Its DNA and scales showed it was different from similar snakes, and the name honors Slash's lifelong love of reptiles.

perspectives.description: Naming a snake after Slash is a cool way to get kids excited about snakes, museums and science.
Others think animals should get names that describe what they look like or where they live, not names of famous people.

perspectives.perspective: Scientists stay focused on the facts
perspectives.description: For the researchers, the name is just a label — the real work was proving with DNA and scales that this snake is a species nobody had ever described before.
